answer: The engineer walks the aqueduct after every crossing and checks each arch for cracks, and the register holds the inspection for the year. A tundra crossing claimed as inspected fails the register: the arches must have been walked at the sonnet of the inspection, and a crossing never inspected has no cracks to report. Buying a false inspection costs a forger 16,700 in bribes to the engineer and a forged register, and the echo register is read before every boat crosses, so an arch whose check was never entered is closed to traffic.
